name: Trillium Arts Individual Artist Residencies 2027
award: $700 honorarium and a seven-night stay in a private suite in Mars Hill, NC
eligibility: Artists 21 and older at any stage of their career; applicants outside the US cover their own travel and visa costs.
note: A week of quiet studio time in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Applying is free; an optional mentorship add-on costs $75.

name: Trillium Arts "Miss Sarah" Fellowship for Black Women Writers
award: $1,000 stipend, a ten-day solo residency with housing, a rental car, and US travel covered
eligibility: Black women writers at any stage of their career; the 2027 fellowship focuses on nonfiction.
note: A July residency near Asheville, NC. Theses, dissertations and edited collections are not eligible.

name: Writers of the Future Contest (Q1 2027)
award: $1,000, $750 and $500 each quarter, plus a $5,000 annual grand prize
eligibility: Writers who haven't professionally published a novel, more than one novelette, or more than three short stories. Science fiction, fantasy or light horror up to 17,000 words; AI-generated work is not accepted.
note: A long-running quarterly contest judged anonymously by professional writers. Entrants keep all publication rights.
disclaimer: Started by L. Ron Hubbard and sponsored by Galaxy Press, the publisher of his fiction. Some writers avoid it because of its ties to the Church of Scientology, which Hubbard founded; the contest says it has no connection to the church.

name: Steinbeck Fellowship (San José State University)
eligibility: Emerging writers of fiction, drama, creative nonfiction or biography (no poetry); fellows must live in the San Francisco Bay Area or nearby counties during the fellowship and not be enrolled in a degree program.
note: Relocation required. The official page lists the deadline as "January 4" without a year; confirm before applying.

name: Poetry magazine
award: $500 per poem; prose $400 per published page
eligibility: Previously unpublished, human-written poetry, translations and prose on poetry; work posted online counts as published.
note: Free to submit. Closed every year from June 15 to September 15.

name: Rattle
award: $200 per poem in print, $100 per poem online
eligibility: Unpublished poems, translations and book reviews; up to four poems at a time. Poems posted on your own social media or blog are fine.
note: Open year-round and always free. Rights revert to the author on publication.

name: The Baltimore Review
note: Regular submissions are free; only its contests charge fees.

name: The Hudson Review (fiction)
eligibility: Writers of any age, background or publication history, US or international; unpublished stories under 10,000 words. No simultaneous submissions.
note: Fiction reads September 1 to November 30, online or by mail. No submission fees.

name: The Yale Review (nonfiction)
award: $250 to $1,000 for prose, depending on length
eligibility: Unpublished nonfiction in English, including pitches; previously posted work (blogs, Substack) doesn't qualify.
note: Nonfiction is free to submit by email. Poetry submissions charge $3, so this listing covers nonfiction only.

name: Redivider (Emerson College)
eligibility: Anyone except current Emerson students, faculty and staff (graduates wait three years); unpublished work.
note: Fiction, flash, poetry, memoir, cultural critique and cover art. Authors keep copyright.

name: Guernica
award: Publication; pay not stated for general submissions
eligibility: Unpublished fiction (2,000–7,000 words), nonfiction (2,500+ words) and poetry (up to five poems).
note: A respected magazine of art and politics. Poems are exclusive to Guernica for 90 days, then non-exclusive.

name: The Offing
eligibility: Unpublished work; open departments are Insight (essays up to 5,000 words), Micro (any genre, 10–560 characters) and Art & Comics.
note: Free to submit through 2026, thanks to donors. Fiction and poetry departments are currently closed.

name: AGNI (by mail)
award: $30 per page for prose, $50 per page for poetry (up to $300)
eligibility: Writers of any identity, location or publication history; unpublished work in English.
note: Free only when sent on paper by mail; submitting online costs $3. Reading period runs to December 15.

name: Sierra Nevada Review
eligibility: Unpublished poetry, fiction and nonfiction; one submission per reading period. Writers keep all rights.
note: The University of Nevada, Reno at Lake Tahoe journal, reading for its Spring 2027 issue.

name: Michigan Quarterly Review: MQR Online
eligibility: Pitches for essays, book reviews, arts and culture features and author interviews; selected pitches are invited to submit up to 3,000 words.
note: Online pitches are free year-round. The print journal and its prizes charge fees, so use the MQR Online category.

name: Barrelhouse: newsletter essays
eligibility: Unpublished personal essays about a pop-culture obsession, under 1,000 words (strict).
note: Accepted on a rolling basis but may pause when the queue fills. Rights return to the author after the newsletter goes out.
